attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, endorsed in his voice.

semantics.note: The firm part (works very poorly and inconsistently) is an observation about the launch product. The proposition keeps 'likely very expensive' as 'probably', so that hedged part stays unscored. Turning 'very very' into 'very' softens it a little but is acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading (frequent substantive failures and unreliable completion of advertised tasks in the launch period) is a fair, ordinary reading of 'very very poorly and inconsistently'. It correctly leaves the hedged cost remark out of the scoring and invents no numerical threshold.

evidence.note: Independent hands-on review from launch week. It finds the agent sluggish, not always reliable and glitchy, which supports 'inconsistently'. But it is one small sample, and it says the agent usually gets part or most of the job done, so it falls short of showing 'very very poorly' across ordinary tasks.

OpenAI's own launch disclosure of benchmark scores (e.g., 68.9% on BrowseComp). It is a company statement, not an independent finding, and does not show dependable completion of ordinary tasks or consistency across repeated tries.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs representative evaluations of the launch version. The packet has one small independent hands-on test that supports unreliability but describes partial success, plus company benchmarks that only add context. The packet itself admits it lacks a representative launch-era evaluation with repeated trials. That is not enough to establish or refute 'very very poorly and inconsistently' across ordinary advertised tasks. The cost remark is hedged and not scored.
